result.title: Removing the Compute Bottleneck for Event-based Visual Place Recognition with Spiking Neural Networks
result.summary: Neuromorphic sensing and computing promise low latency and high energy efficiency for robotics, yet most event-based visual place recognition (VPR) pipelines reintroduce dense, frame-like computation downstream of an inherently sparse sensor, forfeiting the sensor's latency advantage. In this paper, we address the problem of resolving an event-based VPR query in tens of microseconds on a commodity CPU. We train a two-layer spiking neural network (SNN) with additive spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), which drives the learned weight matrix towards a strongly bimodal distribution, amenable to aggressive magnitude pruning. At inference, our pipeline exploits this sparsity by reading only the pruned weights corresponding to the query's active pixels. As surviving weights share a near-uniform magnitude, each neuron's score reduces to an integer count of matching synapses instead of a weighted sum, lowering per-query latency. This computation is small enough to remain resident in a CPU's fast on-chip cache. On three event-based VPR benchmarks, our sparse SNN exceeds the recall of LENS, an existing event-based SNN, while reducing per-query latency by 5.5-6.2x to tens of microseconds. It matches the recall of a dense variant of our network and of the sum-of-absolute-differences (SAD) baseline, while reading 10x fewer weights than the dense variant. We further characterise how recall and latency scale with the number of active pixels and reference places. These results suggest that the sparsity of both event-based input and learned weights can already be exploited for low-latency inference on conventional processors.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对事件相机视觉地点识别（VPR），用附加 STDP 训练两层 SNN 使权重呈双峰分布后做激进幅度剪枝，推理时仅读取查询活跃像素对应的存活权重、把神经元打分退化为整数计数，从而在通用 CPU 上以数十微秒完成检索；在三个基准上召回超过 LENS，延迟降低 5.5–6.2 倍，并刻画了召回与延迟随活跃像素数和参考地点数的伸缩关系。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其「按输入活跃度稀疏读取权重、以匹配计数替代加权求和」的推理方式，以及召回–延迟随活跃像素/参考规模的伸缩分析，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与动态计算成本评估提供参照，是否可迁移需核查。
